name: dev.telara/slack-standup-digest
description: Scan a Slack channel's recent history and, when a standup thread is present, its replies, then extract per-person yesterday/today/blockers fields from the free-text posts using a schema-constrained reasoning step. Author and channel identity are resolved deterministically before any reasoning runs. Extractions below a confidence threshold are routed to unparsed_messages rather than trusted. Read-only; never posts, edits, or reacts to anything.

transform.program:
# pick_thread.star -- deterministic selection of the one standup thread (if
# any) to expand this run. TAP transform contract: step params arrive as
# predeclared globals (messages, explicit_thread_ts); the value assigned to
# `result` is the step's output. No I/O, no imports.
#
# Slack sets a message's thread_ts equal to its own ts exactly when that
# message is the root of a thread with replies (conversations.history docs).
# That is known-field matching, not semantic extraction -- the same
# deterministic-first discipline as gitlab-pipeline-triage's signature table,
# just over a boolean/equality field instead of a string enum.
#
# SCOPE DECISION (see README): today's engine has no per-item fan-out step
# type, so a single static workflow cannot call list_thread_replies once per
# thread root found in list_messages. This primitive resolves at most one
# thread per run: an explicit thread_ts input wins; otherwise the most
# recently active thread root in the scanned window is used.

def _is_thread_root(m):
    ts = m.get("ts")
    thread_ts = m.get("thread_ts")
    return ts != None and thread_ts != None and thread_ts == ts

def _pick(messages, explicit_thread_ts):
    if explicit_thread_ts:
        return explicit_thread_ts
    roots = [m for m in messages if _is_thread_root(m)]
    if len(roots) == 0:
        return None
    best = roots[0]
    for r in roots[1:]:
        if r["ts"] > best["ts"]:
            best = r
    return best["ts"]

result = {"thread_ts": _pick(messages, explicit_thread_ts)}

model.prompt: Perform the workflow reasoning task: extract_standup_fields_from_free_text

transform.program:
# gate.star -- deterministic confidence gate. Predeclared params: candidates
# (from resolve_candidates.star), reasoned (list from extract_fields, or None
# when that step was skipped because there were no candidates), channel,
# thread_ts, min_confidence. Output via `result`.
#
# Gate rule: a reasoned extraction below min_confidence, OR a candidate the
# lease didn't return a matching row for at all, is routed to
# unparsed_messages -- never silently trusted or folded into digest. This is
# the same "model output is bounded by a deterministic gate" discipline as
# gitlab-pipeline-triage's verdict.star, applied to every candidate rather
# than only to a signature-unmatched residue, because here every candidate's
# fields come from the lease (there is no deterministic classification path
# for free text -- see README).

def _reasoned_lookup(reasoned):
    m = {}
    if reasoned == None:
        return m
    for r in reasoned:
        m[r["ts"]] = r
    return m

def _gate(candidates, reasoned, channel, thread_ts, min_confidence):
    rmap = _reasoned_lookup(reasoned)
    digest = []
    unparsed = []
    for c in candidates:
        r = rmap.get(c["ts"])
        if r == None:
            unparsed.append({
                "user_id": c["user_id"],
                "display_name": c["display_name"],
                "source": c["source"],
                "posted_at": c["ts"],
                "text": c["text"],
                "confidence": 0.0,
                "reason": "extraction_incomplete",
            })
            continue
        conf = r.get("confidence", 0.0)
        if conf >= min_confidence:
            digest.append({
                "user_id": c["user_id"],
                "display_name": c["display_name"],
                "source": c["source"],
                "posted_at": c["ts"],
                "yesterday": r.get("yesterday"),
                "today": r.get("today"),
                "blockers": r.get("blockers"),
                "confidence": conf,
            })
        else:
            unparsed.append({
                "user_id": c["user_id"],
                "display_name": c["display_name"],
                "source": c["source"],
                "posted_at": c["ts"],
                "text": c["text"],
                "confidence": conf,
                "reason": "below_confidence_threshold",
            })
    return {
        "digest": digest,
        "unparsed_messages": unparsed,
        "summary": {
            "channel": channel,
            "thread_id": thread_ts,
            "total_candidates": len(candidates),
            "parsed_count": len(digest),
            "unparsed_count": len(unparsed),
        },
    }

result = _gate(candidates, reasoned, channel, thread_ts, min_confidence)

inputs.name: channel
inputs.description: Slack channel ID whose recent activity is scanned for standup posts

inputs.name: latest
inputs.description: Slack timestamp upper bound of the scan window; omitted scans through the most recent message

inputs.name: max_messages
inputs.description: Cap on standup candidates considered per run, after bot/system-message filtering

inputs.name: oldest
inputs.description: Slack timestamp lower bound of the scan window; omitted scans from retained history start

inputs.name: thread_ts
inputs.description: Optional explicit standup-thread parent timestamp; when omitted, the most recently active thread root found in the scanned window (if any) is used instead
